text: In the Beltrami–Klein and Poincaré disk models of hyperbolic geometry, through a point not on a given line there pass:
explanation: The hyperbolic parallel axiom says at least two — hence infinitely many — lines through the point miss the given line, and the disk models make this visible (open chords, or boundary-perpendicular arcs). 'No parallels at all' describes elliptic geometry; 'exactly one' is the Euclidean/Playfair case.
